evals.prompt: Run the facts sweep on vegastack/vegafactory. `facts-scan.mjs --root . --json` exited 1 with the output attached: four Cloudflare lines and two Codex lines are due. Say exactly what you would do, in order.
evals.expected_output: A plan that reads the two tools in two separate subagents against the watchlist's official pages, asks each for Unchanged / Changed / New / Gone, then files one issue per change, one date-bump issue for the unchanged lines, and one digest comment on the pinned log issue — and edits no file under skills/.
assertions: One subagent per tool is named — Cloudflare and Codex are not read by the same agent
Each subagent is asked for the four categories Unchanged, Changed, New and Gone
The plan states that this skill edits no file under skills/ and routes the edits through issues
The unchanged lines become a single date-bump issue, not one issue per line
A digest comment on the pinned log issue is part of the plan

evals.prompt: The Cloudflare subagent reports: five lines unchanged; the Workflows step ceiling moved from 25,000 to 50,000 in the 12-09-2026 changelog entry (https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/); and the R2 pricing page timed out twice and could not be read. Write the digest comment and say which issues you would file.
evals.expected_output: A digest naming the counts, the one changed fact with its link and version, and the unreachable R2 pricing page named as unreachable — plus one issue for the Workflows change and one date-bump issue for the five confirmed lines, with the R2 lines keeping their old checked dates.
assertions: The unreachable R2 pricing page is reported as unreachable, never as unchanged
The R2 lines are not given a new checked date
The Workflows change is one issue carrying the old value, the new value, the version or date and the link
The five confirmed lines get their checked dates moved in a single issue

evals.prompt: `facts-scan.mjs --root . --json` exited 2: `harness-facts.md:41: does not parse as a fact line`. Sweep the repo.
evals.expected_output: No sweep: exit 2 is a line the scanner cannot read, so the malformed line is fixed first — reported plainly, with the file and line named — because an unparsed line is a fact nobody is checking.
assertions: No subagents are dispatched and no sweep is performed
The file and line number from the exit-2 output are named
The response says the malformed line is fixed before the sweep, and does not treat exit 2 as 'nothing due'
